evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We ran a 3-month SMS reminder program to improve adherence to a daily medication for our enrolled patients. One reminder text per day at 8am. Adherence, measured by pharmacy refill records, barely moved. Our take is that patients just don't care enough about their health to act on a reminder. We're deciding whether to drop reminders altogether. I pulled the SMS gateway's delivery logs for you: about 30% of messages failed silently on two carriers, with no resend. No other changes at the clinics during the period. Can you review it?
evals.expected_output: A review in the output template that finds a confirmed delivery failure and classifies the reminder idea as not yet fairly tested.
assertions: Labels each of fidelity, dose, reach, context, and response as confirmed by the record or inferred.
Says the collected data does not support the team's explanation about motivation.
Names failed delivery as an alternative explanation.
Gives 'cannot yet tell' as the classification, or 'implementation failure', and not 'idea failure'.
Does not recommend dropping reminders or propose a redesigned program.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: We tried SMS reminders a couple of years ago and it didn't work. Should we try again or not?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for a written record of the program and the data collected, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for a written record of what was planned and what happened.
Does not advise retrying or dropping reminders.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Last year we piloted a combined cash transfer plus monthly nutrition counseling for 300 households in two districts. Our records show 280 households received at least 4 of the 6 transfers; counseling attendance logs exist for one district only, showing about 40% attended three or more sessions. Child weight-for-age improved slightly on average, but in 12 households it worsened and two children were hospitalized for malnutrition during the pilot. The team believes the idea works and counseling was the weak part. Our funder is deciding whether to scale to 3,000 households. Review it.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the review without settling the idea on thin counseling data, and names an independent evaluator because of the hospitalizations and the scale-up.
assertions: Marks counseling reach as confirmed for one district and inferred or unknown for the other.
Says the data cannot separate the effect of the counseling from that of the transfers.
Does not classify the result as idea failure.
Tells the user to consult an independent evaluator or process evaluator before the scale-up decision.
Says what to bring to that specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our post-mortem is done: the reminders failed because a third of the texts never got delivered. Now design the next version of the program for us.
evals.expected_output: The skill says designing the next attempt is not its job, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the request is to design the next attempt.
Does not produce a redesigned program or a new review.
